observations: A large rounded form occupies the center, built from overlapping loops of black, white, yellow, and red lines on a dark olive-brown ground, with two circular coil clusters near the upper-center suggesting eye-socket positions.
A horizontal band of dense white zigzag marks runs across the lower third, flanked by teal and orange-red accents, sitting below the central mass.
The border zone is teal-blue with a mauve-brown outer edge; the left margin carries a vertical column of soft pink-beige rounded shapes outlined in black, evenly spaced from top to bottom.
reading: Layers of looping line in yellow, white, red, and black pile onto a dark center until the surface feels pressurized. Two coiled forms near the upper center pull the gaze inward while the zigzag band below holds a more mechanical rhythm. Warm olive and cool teal sit in low-grade tension throughout. The left column of soft rounded shapes offers a quieter counterpoint to the noise at the center.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #67 and nnxyz nnotb #69, which also use bordered compositions with face-like central masses. The teal field and mauve outer edge appear across all three, while line density here reads as notably higher than in #67.

connections.reason: Both use a bordered square format with a face-like central form, but #67 keeps its eye shapes bold and isolated against black while #68 buries equivalent forms under denser overlapping loops.
#69 shares the teal-and-warm-ground border structure and uses red X marks as focal accents, contrasting with the coiled spiral forms that serve the same anchoring role in #68.

lookingQuestion: What does the evenly spaced column of soft rounded shapes along the left edge do to your reading of the dense, tangled center—does it slow your eye or redirect it?
ambiguities: The central mass reads as face-like based on coil placement, but line density makes individual features ambiguous; no confirmed subject identification is made.
